column.text: Institutional money is heading for the exits. Bitcoin ETFs lost $239.9M on Tuesday 17 Nov, pushing the seven-day net to -$1,297.4M. Ether ETFs gave up $29.1M that same Tuesday, with a seven-day net of -$436.4M. Solana's seven-day net is -$20.4M, and it recorded no inflow on Tuesday. Price confirms the pressure. Bitcoin closed at $63,184, down 1.32%, and total crypto market cap fell 4.95%. Fear & Greed sits at 11, deep in Extreme Fear. BTC has held above its 30-day swing low at 62,006 but has broken below S1 at 63,706 and lost its pivot. ETH is sitting on its S1 at 1,769.68, with its 30-day low at 1,711.08 just beneath. The dominant risk is a long-liquidation cascade. Bitcoin's long/short ratio is 2.63, with 72.5% of positions long, so a move through the $62,000 to $62,500 zone could force a fast unwind. The regime is risk-off and the trend is down, so continuation shorts carry the momentum. Any short needs a tight stop above R1, and conviction is only 6 out of 10, so size accordingly. Longs need a real mechanism: deeply negative funding, a capitulation reading, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown. A dip that merely looks oversold does not qualify. Dollar liquidity is flat, so there is no macro tailwind either way. Trade the structure. Watch whether BTC can reclaim S1 at 63,706; a failure there keeps the 62,006 swing low in play.
